relationships.title: Galactic Core
relationships.description: A supermassive Black Hole centers most Galaxies, its immense gravity holding billions of stars in orbital dance.

relationships.title: Stellar Birth
relationships.description: When a star explodes as a Supernova, it creates a Nebula - a cosmic nursery where new stars are born from the scattered material.

relationships.title: Stellar Death
relationships.description: The most massive Supernovas collapse into Black Holes, creating regions where gravity is so strong that not even light can escape.

relationships.title: Neutron Star Formation
relationships.description: Pulsars are born from Supernovas, rapidly spinning neutron stars that emit beams of radiation like cosmic lighthouses.

relationships.title: Star Formation Regions
relationships.description: Nebulas form within Galaxies as clouds of gas and dust, creating the colorful regions where new stars ignite.

relationships.title: Crew Transport
relationships.description: Rockets deliver astronauts and supplies to the Space Station, maintaining humanity's permanent presence in orbit.

relationships.title: Orbital Network
relationships.description: Satellites orbit alongside the Space Station, forming a network of scientific instruments and communication relays.

relationships.title: Mars Mission
relationships.description: Advanced Rockets travel to Mars, carrying rovers and equipment to explore the red planet's surface.

relationships.title: Rocky vs Icy
relationships.description: Asteroids are rocky bodies while Comets are icy, but both are ancient remnants from the solar system's formation.

relationships.title: Primordial Material
relationships.description: Comets contain pristine material from the Nebula that formed our solar system, frozen time capsules from 4.6 billion years ago.

relationships.title: Lunar Gateway
relationships.description: The Moon serves as a stepping stone to Mars, where we test technologies and train for deep space exploration.

relationships.title: Space Weather
relationships.description: Solar Flares threaten Satellites with intense radiation and electromagnetic pulses that can damage electronics.

relationships.title: Spacetime Tunnel
relationships.description: Wormholes are theorized to connect distant Black Holes, creating shortcuts through spacetime itself.

relationships.title: Invisible Scaffolding
relationships.description: Dark Matter binds Galaxies together with invisible gravity, making up 85% of the universe's mass.

relationships.title: Einstein-Rosen Bridge
relationships.description: Some theories suggest Black Holes may connect to Wormholes, creating bridges between different regions of spacetime.

relationships.title: Cosmic GPS
relationships.description: Pulsars can navigate Satellites like cosmic GPS, their precise timing helping spacecraft determine position in deep space.

relationships.title: Crater Formation
relationships.description: Asteroids have impacted Mars throughout history, creating the massive craters that cover the red planet's surface.

relationships.title: Lunar Research
relationships.description: The Space Station observes the Moon, studying its geology and testing technologies for future lunar bases.

relationships.title: Gravitational Dance
relationships.description: Dark Matter interacts with Black Holes through gravity, influencing how matter falls into the event horizon.

relationships.title: Intergalactic Bridge
relationships.description: Wormholes could theoretically connect distant Galaxies, allowing instantaneous travel across cosmic distances.
